segments.title: Kendall's Basketball Trivia Crisis
segments.notes: Kendall interrupts the open to demand chat identify basketball players 'Yanis' and 'Yo Kitch' (Giannis Antetokounmpo and Nikola Jokić) for a podcast she's speed-listening to.

segments.title: Subs, Hype Train, and Jeff Ripple Returns
segments.notes: Case thanks sub gifters tamtran, commander gab, and daddy; a level-two Hype Train completes unnoticed; Jeff Ripple crashes the desk uninvited to announce his Twitch Partner application.

segments.title: Sports Illustrated AI Writers Exposed
segments.notes: Jeff Ripple spirals over Futurism's investigation revealing Sports Illustrated published articles by AI-generated personas (Drew Ortiz, Sora Tanaka, Domino Abrams) with headshots sourced from an AI face website; Jeff takes it as an existential threat to journalism.

segments.title: President Biden on AI and Ice Cream Dimples
segments.notes: Case summons a Biden impression who declares AI illegal, insists his house stay 'dumb and white,' and recounts his granddaddy licking his face clean while calling him 'loads a j buddy.'

segments.title: Trump Calls In: Scalp Haircuts and Robot Parts
segments.notes: A Trump impression enters boasting about a right-side scalp haircut, challenges robots to trade pectoral muscles for legs, claims ironic-detachment superiority over Nicolas Cage, and ambiguously places himself at the Capitol on January 6.

segments.title: Go to the Movies: Lady Ballers, Napoleon, Book of Clarence, Super Fast
segments.notes: Trent and Chris (Case personas) review trailers: Daily Wire's 'Lady Ballers' (anti-trans sports comedy with Ben Shapiro, Jordan Peterson, Ted Cruz), Ridley Scott's 'Napoleon' (Joaquin Phoenix voice mocked), biblical dramedy 'Book of Clarence' (Jesus has superpowers), and Friedberg/Seltzer's final spoof 'Super Fast' (no nut shot, franchise retired).

segments.title: Kendall Interviews a Basketball
segments.notes: Kendall questions a basketball (chat roleplay) about rookie 'Wenby' (Victor Wembanyama), top players (Giannis, Jokić, Luka, KD, Curry, Edwards, Dame), LeBron/Steph rivalry, and correct PSI (7.5–8.5).

segments.title: Dick News Trilogy: Disney Streaker, Frozen Penis, Chandler Jones
segments.notes: Case and Jeff cover three penis stories: a man streaking It's a Small World at Disneyland (fully nude, carried out by security), Finnish skier Cal Halvorsen's frostbitten penis (Prince Harry memoir callback), and Raiders ex-Chandler Jones flashing 'penis meat' in a bathroom mirror video.

segments.title: Toad vs Birdo: Mario Kart Hotness Debate
segments.notes: Munch argues Birdo's suction-mouth superiority; Crum defends Toad's humanoid consent capacity; Munch plays his theme song, Crum updates score to 69–60, both claim victory.

segments.title: Fiona's Dog Producer Poll and Raid to John Madison
segments.notes: Fiona's Dog (chupacabra-adjacent desert dog) wins producer poll via paw-instinct; Case raids longtime friend John Madison (twitch.tv/jonmadison) who is sketching imaginary worlds on AM radio.

characters.name: Kendelle
characters.notes: in-studio contributor. Derails the cold open demanding chat identify NBA players Giannis Antetokounmpo and Nikola Jokić for a podcast, later interviews a sentient basketball.

characters.name: Jeff Ripple
characters.notes: correspondent. Crashes the desk to announce Partner application, then spirals over Sports Illustrated's AI-generated authors before co-hosting the penis-news block.

characters.name: Chet (Chet Manscape)
characters.notes: science correspondent. Closes the dick-news segment as Chet Manscape, offering insulated-underwear hope to 'little penises' freezing in the steerage of the Titanic.

characters.name: Munch (Ralph Munchcut)
characters.notes: debate analyst. Champions Birdo's mouth mechanics in the Mario Kart hotness debate, plays his victory song, and leads the score 69–60.

characters.name: Crum (Leonard Crum)
characters.notes: debate analyst. Defends Toad's humanoid consent viability, accuses Munch of cheating, and narrows the score gap to under 20 points.

characters.name: Fiona's Dog
characters.notes: producer candidate. Wins the producer poll with paw-instinct qualifications, reveals chupacabra anatomy (bird feathers, rooster legs), and barks the sign-off.

storylines.beat: [126:58] Munch suggests Crum needs 'a hot round of Beyblade' as the show exits, referencing the pending 2v2 Beyblade Burst Event pledge.

lore_notes.fact: Case Blackwell is fasting on broadcast day.
Munch & Crum debate score updated: Munch 69, Crum ~50 (under 20 points behind).
Fiona's Dog wins producer poll and is canonically a chupacabra-adjacent desert dog with bird feathers and rooster legs.
Raid target: John Madison (twitch.tv/jonmadison), Case's longtime friend formerly known as Daniel Spaniel.

episode_summary: Case Blackwell anchors a frenetic broadcast that opens with Kendall's NBA trivia emergency, spirals through Jeff Ripple's existential crisis over AI-generated Sports Illustrated authors, and features dueling presidential impressions declaring war on artificial intelligence. The 'Go to the Movies' segment dissects Daily Wire's 'Lady Ballers' alongside Napoleon, Book of Clarence, and the final Friedberg/Seltzer spoof Super Fast. A basketball Q&A, a three-story penis-news block (Disney streaker, Finnish frostbite, Chandler Jones), and a Munch & Crum debate on Toad vs Birdo hotness precede Fiona's Dog winning the producer poll and a raid on friend John Madison.
